newsitem.title: USA: Goldman relatives file to split Simpson damages.
newsitem.headline: Goldman relatives file to split Simpson damages.

text.p: Family members of murder victim Ronald Goldman on Wednesday made their first move toward collecting the millions of dollars in damages they won from O.J. Simpson, filing a proposal to finalise the judgment.

The proposal calls for the slain man's father, Fred Goldman, to get 85 percent of the compensatory damages, or around $7.2 million, while his mother, Sharon Rufo, would get 15 percent or about $1.3 million.
The papers were filed after attorneys for Goldman and Rufo met behind closed doors to hammer out an agreement on how the damages should be split.
Fred Goldman and Sharon Rufo divorced in 1974 and Rufo had little contact with her son or daughter, Kim. Ronald Goldman was murdered on June 12, 1994.

A civil court jury found Simpson responsible for the murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and Goldman, and awarded Goldman's parents $8.5 million in compensatory damages on Feb 4. Six days later they added punitive damages of $12.5 million, with another $12.5 million to be paid to the estate of Simpson's ex-wife.
Under California law, Fred Goldman and Sharon Rufo must split the punitive damages equally.

The proposed judgment filed on Wednesday by Goldman marks the first step in the legal skirmish that is expected to follow the verdicts against the ex-American football star who was acquitted of the murders by a criminal court jury in October 1995.
Once Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki reviews and signs the judgment, Simpson is alotted 15 days to file papers asking the judge to overturn the verdicts or reduce the damages.
To lodge an appeal Simpson would have to post a bond of 1-1/2 times the total amount of damages or around $50 million.
His attorney for the appeal, Dan Leonard, did not return calls to his Boston office seeking comment.
Fred Goldman, in an interview on Cable News Network, said he was prepared for whatever legal hurdles were ahead.
"We're in a fight until it's over," he said. "If there's an appeal, there's an appeal, but I don't think Judge Fujisaki committed any errors that will reverse the decisions."
Rufo, in an interview aired on KCAL-TV, said her lack of contact with Ron had not made his death any easier to bear.
"Any parent who has lost a child feels pain," she said. "I can only assume that Mr. Goldman realises that I am feeling pain and hurt and his suffering is no more than mine."
